difficulty_reason: Judged on what the derivation actually carries, not on the proof being printed. The load-bearing steps are: (i) sample t hosts uniformly and independently WITH REPLACEMENT and take their common neighbourhood A - the induced correlation between the host set and A is the design decision that makes the method work, and r=1 exposes why an unconditioned vertex choice fails; (ii) convert the average-degree hypothesis into E|A| = sum_v (deg(v)/n)^t >= n((1/n) sum_v deg(v)/n)^t >= n alpha^t, where the convexity step is applied in the non-obvious direction to turn an average of powers into a power of an average; (iii) for fixed R compute P(R subset A) = (|N(R)|/n)^t and sum over the binom(n,r) bad r-subsets, which requires separating the random A from the fixed test set R; (iv) alter by deleting one vertex per bad r-subset, which destroys every bad subset at a cost bounded by the expected number of such subsets. Steps (i), (iii) and (iv) are specific to this construction rather than generic probabilistic-method background: the unit supplies a concrete, problem-specific mechanism whose design the reader could not read off any standard toolkit statement. That meets the H2 bar as applied elsewhere in this corpus (a printed author construction counted when the construction itself, not its verification, is the non-routine content). It is not H3: the construction is canonical in the field, the section presents it as the introduction of a known technique, and no research-level combination is required.
